claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for child benefit. Let me first review the official eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've reviewed the eligibility criteria. To help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a 16-year-old, Alex, who lives with me at home. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have Alex, who is 16 years old and lives with you.

Since Alex is 16, I need to ask: Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, college courses, or an apprenticeship)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure to be honest. Alex finished school but I don't think they're in any formal college courses or A-levels at the moment. They might be looking at options, but nothing's started yet as far as I know.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So to confirm, Alex has finished school and is not currently enrolled in any approved education or training?

Do you know if Alex has registered with a government-sponsored careers service or is considering joining the armed services?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. They're just at home at the moment, trying to figure out what they want to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Is Alex currently working? If so, do you know how many hours per week they work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at the moment. They're just at home with me while they figure out their next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. One more question: Is Alex claiming any benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits themselves. They're not claiming anything in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Just a couple of final questions to complete my assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. And no, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: While Child Benefit is normally paid for children under 16, it can continue for young people aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training (such as A-levels, college courses, or apprenticeships). Additionally, if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex is 16 and is not currently:
- Enrolled in approved education or training, AND
- Registered with a careers service or the armed services

You would not qualify for Child Benefit at this time.

**However**, if Alex's situation changes - for example, if they:
- Enrol in college, sixth form, or an apprenticeship
- Register with a careers service

You may become eligible to claim Child Benefit again. If either of these happens, you should contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your eligibility.

For children aged 16 or over, the claimant will normally still qualify if the child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Additionally, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. In this case, Alex is 16 years old and: (1) is not currently in approved education or training, (2) has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service, (3) has not registered with the armed services, (4) is not working 24 hours or more per week, and (5) is not claiming benefits in their own right. Since Alex does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit after age 16 (not in approved education/training and not registered with careers service or armed services), the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.
